references.text: The Lord gives Moses a similar command to Aaron to stretch out his staff over the waters of Egypt, resulting in the first plague of blood.
Aaron uses the staff as a sign of God's power, as he does here with the plague of frogs.
Moses stretches out his staff toward the sky to bring hail upon Egypt, a similar pattern where the staff is used as an instrument of God's judgment.
Moses stretches out his staff to bring the plague of locusts upon Egypt, following the same pattern of using the staff as an instrument for plagues.
The psalmist recalls the plague of frogs as part of God's mighty deeds in Egypt.
The psalm describes how frogs swarmed throughout Egypt, even in the king's chambers, serving as a reminder of this plague.
Revelation mentions unclean spirits like frogs, an image that links back to the plague of frogs in Egypt as a symbol of God's judgment.
Theological parallel: God's hand over the water leads to Egypt's downfall (frogs/blood versus drowning).
Direct reference back to the Nile plagues (including frogs) and the use of the staff.
Narrative context: 8:1 introduces the plague, while this verse describes prayer for its end.
Fulfillment of prophecy: The plague of frogs is an example of the 'strong hand' mentioned here.
